newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss industrial investment growth slowing -survey.
newsitem.headline: Swiss industrial investment growth slowing -survey.

text.p: Swiss investment growth will slow in 1997 as companies remain generally wary about spending on new plant and equipment, the Swiss Institute for Business Cycle Research (KOF) found in its annual survey of 2,640 companies.

Weak economic development and the continuing recession in construction industries amid a hesitant global economic upturn had a dampening effect on business expectations and investment plans, the institute said.

"The weakening of dynamism will thus continue in 1997," it said, but added investment remained at a high level and would be helped by spending in the services sector, especially by the federal PTT (post, telephone and telegraph) and the federal railways."
"In contrast with private-sector investment that concentrates on equipment, these agencies plan to invest increasingly in plant," KOF said without giving figures.
Slowing growth was reflected in the negative balance between increases and decreases in investment by industry, the first such negative level since 1992.

Excess capacity in the construction sector was also weighing on investment. "Although there is not such strong pressure to save on investment as there was in 1996, there is no recovery in sight in the construction sector."
Planned cuts in investment budgets tend to curb spending on plant more than on equipment, it said, adding: "The contradictory development in investment on equipment and on plant is continuing."
